course_name_original: Cálculo y Diseño de Máquinas II
prerequisites: Having completed Elasticity and Strength of Materials
Having completed Machine Calculation and Design I

learning_outcomes.text: Know and be able to select the different types of welding.
Know and be able to analyze transmission kinematics.
Be able to describe the operating modes of a plain surface bearing and describe the conditions under which it operates.
Know the design procedures for boundary and full-film lubrication bearings.
Be able to describe a hydrostatic bearing system and its basic design.
Design and analyze compression and extension springs and calculate dimensions for various characteristics.
Know and design industrial lifting and transport equipment in industry and construction.
Know and design a conveyor belt for use in industry and mining.
Know and calculate cables in an industrial context.
Analyze the different parts of an industrial technical design project for a lifting and transport machine.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical Transmission Systems: Basic knowledge
Mechanical Transmission Systems: Kinematic study of transmission
Mechanical Transmission Systems: Design of bevel gears
Mechanical Transmission Systems: Design of helical gears
Bearings: Generalities
Bearings: Design of bearings with boundary lubrication
Bearings: Design of bearings with full-film hydrodynamic lubrication
Bearings: Design of hydrostatic bearings
Springs: Generalities
Springs: Design of helical compression springs
Springs: Design of helical extension springs
Springs: Design of helical torsion springs
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: Description and Types
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: Operating parameters
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: Time to accelerate a load
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: System inertia
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: Energy absorption
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: Response time
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: Materials and friction coefficients
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: Flywheel dynamics
Brakes, Clutches, and Flywheels: Materials
Shaft Couplings: Rigid couplings
Shaft Couplings: Elastic couplings
Shaft Couplings: Mobile couplings
Lifting Cables: Basic notions
Practical: Analysis of reduction gearbox, cardan transmission, and differential mechanism
Practical: Analysis of braking system
Practical: Analysis of a hydrodynamic bearing
Practical: Analysis of springs
assessment_rules: Under the continuous evaluation model, assessment consists of two in-person development tests (90% of the grade, split 40% for the first and 60% for the second) and other continuous assessment activities (10%). A minimum grade of 5 is required for the two development tests to be weighted. Practical sessions must be passed ('APTAS') and are mandatory; failure results in a practical exam, and if its grade is below 5, that becomes the final course grade. Under the single evaluation model, assessment is a single development test (100%), and practical sessions must also be 'APTAS'. In both models, students must demonstrate minimum knowledge in all parts of the final exam to average the grades; otherwise, the final grade will be 4.
